mechanism: Amphotericin B causes significant nephrotoxicity and electrolyte disturbances (hypokalemia, hypomagnesemia) while promethazine's anticholinergic effects and CNS depression may mask symptoms and complicate fluid/electrolyte management.
action: Monitor renal function, electrolytes, and cardiac status closely; use amphotericin B lipid formulations when possible; minimize promethazine use or use alternative antiemetics; assess QT interval given hypokalemia risk.
